the drought tolerance of rootstocks in grapevine is determined by both chemical (i. e., ABA) as well as hydraulic signals (i.e., root system architecture) in stomatal regulation.
(i) the root system architecture, (ii) ABA biosynthesis in the roots and (iii) the hydraulic conductive properties of roots all contribute to the rootstock-specific stomata control.
Rootstocks contribute to the stomatal control of scion under drought through the control of both hydraulic and chemical (ABA) signals.

a better understanding of the role of rootstocks in stomatal control and how rootstocks contribute to drought tolerance in scions.
the identification of root characteristics that are associated with drought tolerance in grapevine, and the integration of root and shoot responses into a transpiration model.
the role of the root system in the regulation of stomata and the contribution of rootstocks to the drought tolerance of grafted grapevines.

The main takeaway from our work is that
rootstock effects on the regulation of stomatal control are mediated by both hydraulic and chemical root-to-shoot signals.

rootstock-specific differences in stomatal regulation are not only due to chemical signals (i.e., xylem sap concentration of ABA), but also to the hydraulic signals (i.e. root hydraulic conductance) that affect the ABA concentration in the xylem sap.
rootstocks can control scion E through the modulation of both hydraulic and chemical components, and that this is achieved by the root architecture and ABA biosynthesis, respectively.
